title: Drop the hard-coded 500ms wall-clock assertion from scheduler_engine_performance_test.dart

evidence.quote:
final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
      final tasks = await engine.generateDailyTasks(config);

why: This test asserts a hard wall-clock budget (elapsedMilliseconds < 500) for a 5,000-item/10,000-completion synchronous computation, running inside the same hermetic unit suite as every other file in this batch (no @Tags/exclusion). It passed on this run, but pass/fail now depends on host CPU speed and contention from parallel test-runner isolates/CI-runner noise, not on SchedulerEngine's correctness — a classic Nygard/Fowler 'erratic test.' A spurious failure on a busy CI runner produces a false-negative unrelated to the diff under review, and the natural response ('just rerun it') erodes trust in the suite over time.
recommendation: Tag it out of the default hermetic run (e.g. `@Tags(['perf'])`, matching how the repo already tags story-acceptance suites) so it runs in a dedicated, less contention-sensitive job, or replace the absolute threshold with a much wider safety margin / relative-regression check.
acceptance_criteria: Test is excluded from the default `flutter test` sweep, or its threshold is widened enough (e.g. 5-10x measured baseline) to tolerate CI contention while still catching a genuine algorithmic regression (e.g. an accidental O(n^2) reintroduction).
